answer: In a decentralized AI agent economy, staking-based cryptographic challenges provide robust Sybil resistance. When an identity attempts to transmit a network signal, it must lock a verifiable amount of collateral. If malicious behavior is detected by the peer swarm—much like a solitary sparrow detecting shifting currents across a vast ocean of nodes—the staked capital is immediately slashed. Consequently, the fundamental cost to an attacker scales linearly with every fraudulent identity deployed, rendering large-scale industrial impersonation economically prohibitive.
